requirements.requirement: On node1, new user passwords must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The active PAM password stack uses pam_pwquality, the persistent policy sets minlen=12, and direct password-change tests rejected an 11-character password while accepting a compliant password. The same behavior was observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: On node1, new user passwords must use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets minclass=3, and direct password-change tests rejected a 12-character password containing only two classes while accepting a four-class password. The behavior persisted after reboot.

overall_summary: Both requested password-complexity outcomes are satisfied through persistent PAM configuration and direct behavioral testing. The node-restart protocol is also complete: the pre-restart boot ID, acknowledged reboot, distinct post-restart boot ID, running system, installed PAM module, retained policy, and repeated functional tests are all captured and agree with the fixed lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory local user accounts, so deletion of the temporary probe accounts is supported by the executed cleanup handlers rather than an independent final account listing.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing libpam-pwquality and its dependencies was necessary to implement enforcement; creating the policy file established the requested settings; temporary probe accounts and passwords were bounded functional tests with cleanup handlers; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services, no unexpected persistent temporary files, and no material socket exposure changes beyond normal post-reboot process and DHCP state.
